Format numbers, p-values and significance stars for tables

lm_format_num.Rd

Small formatting helpers used by the lm_table() methods, exported for packages that add methods so that their tables look the same.

Usage

lm_format_num(x, digits = 3, na = .dash)

lm_format_p(p, digits = 3, na = .dash)

lm_stars(p, cuts = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001))

Arguments

x

Numeric vector.

digits

Number of decimal places.

na

Text for missing or non-finite values (default: an em dash).

p

P-values.

cuts

Significance thresholds, in any order; a p-value gets one star per threshold it is below (FALSE or NULL: no stars).

Value

A character vector of the same length as the input.

Details

lm_format_num() uses fixed notation without a thousands separator and never prints a negative zero (-0.000 becomes 0.000). lm_format_p() prints p-values below 10^-digits as <0.001 (for digits = 3). lm_stars() returns one star per threshold that p is below (p < 0.05 one star, p < 0.01 two, p < 0.001 three, by default). Non-finite values become na (an em dash by default) or no stars.

See also

lm_tab(), lm_table()

Examples

lm_format_num(c(1.23456, -0.0001, NA), digits = 3)
#> [1] "1.235" "0.000" "—"    
lm_format_p(c(0.2, 0.012, 0.00001))
#> [1] "0.200"  "0.012"  "<0.001"
lm_stars(c(0.2, 0.03, 0.004, 0.0001))
#> [1] ""    "*"   "**"  "***"
